title: FHE and plaintext consumer ownership map
scope: Inventory of what the tree contains and who owns it. It qualifies no cryptography, establishes no readiness and grants no runtime permission.

guide.checker: python3 -I -S scripts/check_fhe_ownership_map.py validates this file against the tree; scripts/tests/check_fhe_ownership_map_test.py tests it. Both run in .github/workflows/pr.yml and under `make check-fhe-ownership`.
guide.refresh: `make refresh-fhe-ownership` (python3 scripts/check_fhe_ownership_map.py --refresh --write) recomputes every derived fact (patterns, cfg chains, test_only flags, callers, function lists). It never changes a classification: new files land in the `unclassified` group and new functions under `production_unassigned` or `test_gated_unassigned`, and the check fails until a maintainer moves them.

sections.crates: Dependency layers, lowest first. `depends_on` equals the manifest dependencies on other listed crates.
sections.primitives: Each reusable ring-arithmetic primitive with one owner module of crates/iroha_fhe and every implementation: the canonical source in that crate and the test-only references that remain with their protocols.
sections.distinct_arithmetic: Arithmetic that keeps an algorithm or proof-field owner, with the reason.
sections.protocol_logic: Scheme logic that stays with its protocol, including the thin adapters that bind protocol parameters to the shared kernels and translate their typed errors. `executes` names what a component runs; an empty list means it only validates, derives, encodes or refuses.
sections.test_only_references: Code compiled only for tests or the development-only fixture feature. None of it is a production stack.
sections.function_assignment: Per owner file, the owner of every production function that no primitive or distinct entry claims, and of every test-gated function and inline test module (`mod <name>`). An owner file is a production-compiled Rust file of an `every_function` scope or a file holding a production primitive implementation.
sections.zk_ams_distinct: What stays with ZK-AMS, what it takes from the shared owner, the oracles to preserve, and the checked statement that its production surface executes nothing.
sections.hkdf: The RAM-LFE HKDF backend that R.6 retires, with every user; the genuine plaintext PRF, recorded separately; and every unrelated HKDF use, which must be preserved.
sections.current_state: The four REQ-032 facts, each anchored to source.
sections.generated_consumers: Schemas, fixtures and inventories with a generator or reader as evidence.
sections.file_groups: Every file the scan finds, classified by component and role.

guide.scan_scope: Every tracked or unignored file is scanned except the paths under scan.excluded_paths (this file, its checker and the plan ledger). A Markdown file is listed only when it names the RAM-LFE HKDF backend. Outside the arithmetic scopes, arithmetic that matches no detection pattern is not inventoried: other proof-field arithmetic (Pasta, BN254, the remaining Goldilocks owners that specs/fastpq/shared_backend_inventory.json lists), signature and curve arithmetic, and erasure coding.

Task C.2 then established crates/iroha_fhe and moved the production kernels into it; the owners below are the state after that move. The field is a provenance note and is not refreshed; the checker decides whether the inventory matches the tree.

consumed_by.C.2: established the destination: primitives now name crates/iroha_fhe as canonical source; function_assignment records the adapters left in each consumer file
consumed_by.C.3: built iroha_fhe::bgv on the shared kernels and added iroha_fhe::natural, ::ntt_plan and ::rns_chain; primitives, protocol_logic (rns_bgv), test_only_references and function_assignment record them. The retained BFV entries are unchanged and are not renamed into the RNS-BGV candidate.
consumed_by.C.5: primitives, test_only_references and function_assignment for ZK-AMS, protocol_logic (bgv_mkhe), zk_ams_distinct

development_features.note: Enabled only from dev-dependencies; cfg(any(test, feature = "bfv-test-fixtures")) therefore counts as test-only.

Enabled only from the dev-dependencies of iroha_fhe itself; crates/iroha_fhe/tests/bgv_surface.rs fails when another manifest names it. cfg(any(test, feature = "bgv-test-fixtures")) therefore counts as test-only.

constraints: Depends on no crate above it in `crates`; iroha_crypto, iroha_zkp_halo2 and iroha_core_privacy depend on it, never the reverse.

For the BFV, ZK-AMS, Jindo and Bootle-Lantern consumers it holds parameter-free arithmetic over slices with typed errors; their schemes, parameters, wire types and codecs, key formats, noise accounting and proofs stay with their protocol owners, which bind parameters and translate errors in thin adapters. The one scheme the crate owns is iroha_fhe::bgv (task C.3), the shared RNS-BGV starting candidate; its wire framing, proofs, circuit privacy and policy stay with its consumers.
Scalar code is the semantic reference; the NEON and AVX2 kernels behind the `simd` feature return its words and fall back to it. No Metal or CUDA kernel exists for word-modulus arithmetic yet.
Extraction preserved each caller's representation, centered reconstruction, branch-free fixed-modulus arithmetic and secret clearing; no wire byte or diagnostic changed.

Production dependencies are zeroize, thiserror, blake3 and getrandom; the last two serve iroha_fhe::bgv only (coin expansion, profile identities, operating-system entropy). crates/iroha_fhe/tests/bgv_surface.rs fails when the list changes.

modules.iroha_fhe::modular: Scalar arithmetic modulo a word-sized modulus, primality and primitive-root search.
modules.iroha_fhe::constant_time: Branch-free selects, canonical add and subtract, fixed-modulus Montgomery arithmetic and the centered three-prime CRT.
modules.iroha_fhe::ntt: Radix-2 cyclic transforms, negacyclic twisting and NTT ring products, including the exact CRT convolution.
modules.iroha_fhe::polynomial: Coefficient-form negacyclic polynomial arithmetic and the schoolbook fallback.
modules.iroha_fhe::rns: Modulus-chain validation, residue decomposition, CRT reconstruction, basis extension and limb-major sums.
modules.iroha_fhe::rounding: Explicit centered lifting, scale-and-round, modulus-switch rounding and nearest-integer division.
modules.iroha_fhe::key_switch: Digit decomposition and the digit/key inner product shared by relinearization, Galois and collective key switching.
modules.iroha_fhe::automorphism: Coefficient permutation with sign for X -> X^k and its unit powers.
modules.iroha_fhe::accel: Accelerated slice kernels (NEON, AVX2), their dispatch and the scalar references they must equal.
modules.iroha_fhe::natural: Arbitrary-precision non-negative integers for public quantities.
modules.iroha_fhe::ntt_plan: Precomputed constant-time negacyclic transform of one prime below 2^62.
modules.iroha_fhe::rns_chain: Exact mixed-radix basis conversion and congruence-preserving scale-down over chains of any length.
modules.iroha_fhe::bgv: The exact modular RNS-BGV scheme shared by RAM-LFE and SoraCloud: profiles, keys, encryption, leveled operations, public noise bounds, slot encodings and the cost model. A starting candidate; nothing consumes it yet.

stays_with_zk_ams: multi-key BGV ciphertext and key formats
collective public-key, relinearization, Galois and key-switching protocols
smudged decryption shares and their proofs
noise, security, resource and packing certificates
RNS-native proof relations, qPCS and wire
adopts_shared_owner: adopted by C.2: scalar modular arithmetic, primality and the modulus-product bound used by BgvProfile::validate, PlaintextModulus::residue and the T256 rotation schedule
still to adopt in C.5: NTT, negacyclic products, automorphisms, digit decomposition and key-switch inner products once they become production

production_surface.claim: No ZK-AMS production function implements or executes an NTT, a ring product, key generation, encryption, decryption or key switching, and none implements scalar modular arithmetic: profile validation calls iroha_fhe. The ring arithmetic exists only under #[cfg(test)]; the production surface validates profiles, derives certificates and refuses to prove or verify.
production_surface.checked_as: Every production function under the prefix is assigned in function_assignment; none belongs to a protocol-logic component whose `executes` is non-empty, and no production implementation under the prefix belongs to a primitive outside allowed_primitives.

current_state.claim: `require_production_support` refuses both BFV backends because the exact-lift profile is insecure: its public-key equation is noiseless modulo the plaintext modulus. Removing the refusal would not make it private.
Core rejects Proof-mode policies and receipts with the unavailable-relation error; no execution proof is verified anywhere.
The Signed verification mode and resolver-signed receipt attestations still exist; openings and phone canonicality rely on signatures. R.6 retires them with the backend.

Torii and the Swift, Kotlin, Java and JavaScript SDKs refuse input encryption with the stable code ram_lfe_encryption_unavailable. The Python and C# SDKs carry receipt and policy models only and expose no input-encryption helper.

arithmetic_scopes.reason: Jindo ring owner; reusable kernels consolidate into iroha_fhe. Files holding them are owner files.
Bootle-Lantern ring owner and the Falcon-512 port. Files holding reusable kernels are owner files.
FASTPQ Goldilocks radix-2 transform and scalar field helpers.
FASTPQ transform planner over the Goldilocks trace and LDE domains.
FASTPQ exact-root Goldilocks column transform with CPU fallback.
Jindo ring: consumer of the shared kernels. Every function stays assigned so a kernel re-introduced here is caught.
Jindo profile check: consumer of the shared kernels. Every function stays assigned so a kernel re-introduced here is caught.
Bootle-Lantern ring: consumer of the shared kernels. Every function stays assigned so a kernel re-introduced here is caught.
Bootle-Lantern toolbox: consumer of the shared kernels. Every function stays assigned so a kernel re-introduced here is caught.

primitives.summary: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, exponentiation, inversion and reduction modulo a u64 modulus, total on every input, with a big-endian byte-string reduction.
notes: Every function is total: a zero modulus yields zero or `None`, which carries the contract of the retired `bfv-accel` `*_mod_prime` duplicates.
Canonical operands of an addition or subtraction take the branch-free kernels of iroha_fhe::constant_time; products use a u128 remainder and are not constant-time.
mkhe.rs keeps `mod_add`, `mod_mul`, `mod_pow`, `bytes_mod_u64` and packing.rs keeps `mod_pow_usize` as test-only references; production profile validation calls the shared owner.
The Bootle-Lantern `*_reference_u64` helpers remain its independent test oracles.

primitives.summary: Deterministic Miller-Rabin primality for u64 and bounded deterministic search and validation of primitive roots of even order.
notes: The registered RAM-LFE root table and its lookup order stay with BFV (`negacyclic_ntt_root_for_order_with_candidate_limit`).
mkhe.rs keeps its own Miller-Rabin as a test-only reference.

primitives.summary: In-place radix-2 cyclic number-theoretic transform with bit-reversal and inverse scaling, generic over the modular arithmetic.
notes: `cyclic_ntt_with` is one butterfly schedule over any `ModularArithmetic`: word arithmetic for BFV, Jindo and the exact CRT convolution, branch-free Montgomery arithmetic for Bootle-Lantern.
`cyclic_ntt_in_place` may dispatch to the NEON or AVX2 kernel; `cyclic_ntt_in_place_scalar` is the reference it must equal.
The ZK-AMS transforms are #[cfg(test)]; no ZK-AMS production code runs an NTT.

primitives.summary: Negacyclic ring product per prime limb: psi twist, cyclic transform, pointwise product, inverse transform and untwist, with the forward and inverse negacyclic transforms on their own.
notes: Callers fall back to the schoolbook kernel when no supported root exists; BFV does so in `multiply_rns_limb_negacyclic`.

primitives.summary: Exact integer product through transforms over fixed helper primes followed by CRT recombination and a negacyclic fold.
notes: Compiled unconditionally in iroha_fhe; BFV selects it through `BfvParameters::convolution_backend` under its `bfv-accel` feature.
Bootle-Lantern keeps its own three-prime CRT profile and reconstructs through `CenteredCrt3`.

primitives.summary: Schoolbook negacyclic product in X^n + 1: the deterministic fallback, the reference the transform paths are tested against, and the product of rings too small for a transform. One generic residue kernel serves variable-time word arithmetic and the branch-free fixed-modulus arithmetic.
notes: Retain this path as the independent small oracle for every transform product.

primitives.summary: Coefficient-wise addition, subtraction, negation and scalar multiplication modulo a word modulus, reduction of signed raw coefficients and checked raw addition.
Ordered NTT-friendly prime chains: structural validation in a fixed rule order, the checked u128 product and the bit length of the exact wide product.
notes: iroha_fhe owns the generic validation of an ordered NTT-friendly prime chain and its checked product. `BfvRnsModulusChain` and `BfvRnsPolynomial` stay in iroha_crypto as BFV wire types with their codecs, schema identities, parameter coupling, guard order and diagnostics; the registered RAM-LFE constants, `BgvProfile` and the Jindo and Bootle-Lantern moduli tables stay with their protocols.
mkhe.rs keeps `WideUint` and `modulus_product` as test-only references; production bounds the product through `modulus_product_bit_len` of the shared owner.

primitives.summary: Residue decomposition of coefficient polynomials and mixed-radix CRT reconstruction, canonical and centered.
notes: One mixed-radix reconstruction serves the BFV chain, the exact CRT convolution and the Jindo two-prime ring; its digits live in a clearing scratch buffer.

primitives.summary: Exact CRT basis extension between modulus chains: target-limb with exact quotient correction, and reduction of reconstructed canonical or centered coefficients into target limbs.
notes: ZK-AMS `incremental_source_rns_native_basis_extension_v2` is a test-only publication contract over native limbs, not a second basis-extension kernel.

primitives.summary: Limb-major sum of RNS polynomials. Limb products are composed per limb from ntt.negacyclic_product and polynomial.schoolbook_negacyclic by each protocol.
notes: Limb-major products are composed by each protocol from the per-limb negacyclic kernel; exact corridors between RNS and coefficient operands are BFV protocol logic.

primitives.summary: Centered lifting, nearest-integer division, ceiling division, scale-and-round of signed integers and modulus-switch rounding; ties away from zero.
notes: Rounding is explicit integer arithmetic; no floating point participates. Ties round away from zero and the even-modulus midpoint lifts as positive.
`modulus_switch_round` is plain rounding of the centered lift; no protocol calls it yet (task C.3 consumes it).

primitives.summary: Base-B digit decomposition of polynomial coefficients, least significant digit first.
notes: ZK-AMS gadget and hybrid digit code is #[cfg(test)]; C.5 adopts the shared kernel when its key switching becomes production.

primitives.summary: Accumulation of both ciphertext components over decomposition digits and key-row pairs, used by relinearization and transformed-secret key switching.
notes: Only the accumulation is shared. BFV relinearization keys, MKHE collective evaluated keys, their generation and their wire stay distinct.

primitives.summary: Signed coefficient permutation for X -> X^k in X^n + 1 over any modular arithmetic, validation of automorphism powers and the list of unit powers.
notes: The kernel writes into a caller buffer so BFV keeps its clearing owner for secret-key transforms.

primitives.summary: Branch-free selects and comparison bits, canonical add and subtract, and fixed-modulus Montgomery arithmetic in the ordinary domain.
notes: Moved from Bootle-Lantern with its Montgomery representation (R = 2^64, residues kept in the ordinary domain) and mask-based selects; Bootle-Lantern pins the constants and its `*_reference_u64` oracles check them.
The canonical add and subtract also serve the reduced-operand path of iroha_fhe::modular.

primitives.summary: Branch-free centered three-prime CRT reconstruction into a target modulus from pinned Garner constants.
notes: Moved from Bootle-Lantern `centered_crt_reconstruct_mod_q_v1`; the profile constants stay in Bootle-Lantern.

primitives.summary: Dispatching slice kernels for modular add, subtract, multiply and the transform, with the scalar references they must equal.
notes: Ineligible inputs (short slices, unreduced operands, unsupported moduli, no CPU support) take the scalar path, so every dispatching function equals its `_scalar` reference on all inputs.
No Metal or CUDA kernel exists for word-modulus arithmetic; the TODO sits at the dispatch site in iroha_fhe::ntt::cyclic_ntt_in_place.

primitives.summary: AArch64 NEON kernels: two-lane Montgomery products with R = 2^32, canonical add and subtract, and transform butterflies.
notes: Compiled under the `simd` feature on AArch64. The `try_*` entry points are produced by the `detected!` macro, which the structural scanner does not expand.

primitives.summary: x86-64 AVX2 kernels: four-lane Montgomery products with R = 2^32, canonical add and subtract, and transform butterflies.
notes: Compiled under the `simd` feature on x86-64 and selected by run-time CPU detection. Test builds compile the same source on every architecture: over the CPU's intrinsics on x86-64 and over the lane model of accel/avx2_model.rs elsewhere, so the kernel's schedule is compared with the scalar reference on every host.
The `try_*` entry points are produced by the `detected!` macro, which the structural scanner does not expand.

primitives.summary: Exact non-negative integers of any size for public quantities: modulus products, level capacities and noise bounds. Variable time; never holds a secret.
notes: Used by iroha_fhe::rns_chain for products and reconstruction of public values and by iroha_fhe::bgv for capacities and noise bounds.
Residue arithmetic never goes through this type.

primitives.summary: Precomputed merged negacyclic transform (Longa-Naehrig) for one odd prime below 2^62 on the branch-free Montgomery kernels: natural-order coefficients to bit-reversed evaluations and back, with point-wise product and multiply-accumulate.
notes: Constant-time in coefficient values; the scalar path is the only path for 50 to 60-bit moduli (TODO in the file for accelerated kernels).
Tested against the generic transform of iroha_fhe::ntt in bit-reversed order and against the schoolbook product.

primitives.summary: Arbitrary-chain RNS without u128 reconstruction: exact mixed-radix digits, exact centered and canonical basis conversion into any odd target modulus, and the congruence-preserving exact scale-down (c - t*w)/D used by BGV modulus switching and by the division by the special modulus.
notes: Up to 64 primes below 2^62 per basis; every basis product is odd, so centered representatives are unique and no tie rule is needed.
Branch-free in residue values. RnsBasis::reconstruct_canonical and reconstruct_centered return Natural values and are for public data only.
iroha_fhe::rns keeps the u128 reconstruction for the retained BFV adapters; the BGV path does not call it (tests/bgv_surface.rs).

distinct_arithmetic.reason: Selective port of the rust-fn-dsa Falcon-512 arithmetic: Montgomery NTT modulo q = 12289, the 31-bit-prime RNS big-integer tower of the NTRU solver and the floating-point FFT polynomials of the sampler. The algorithm fixes this arithmetic and Falcon known-answer vectors test it, so it keeps its algorithm-specific owner.

FIPS 204 ML-DSA polynomial arithmetic modulo 8380417 with the standard's zeta table, Montgomery form and rounding decomposition. The signature algorithm specifies it; it keeps its algorithm-specific owner.
Exact multi-precision integer negacyclic square of signed 512-bit coefficients for the norm transcript. It is not modular ring arithmetic and stays with the Bootle-Lantern transcript.
Power-of-two rounding, gamma decomposition and mask decompositions fixed by the Bootle-Lantern proof format. They split residues for compression and reconciliation and are not reusable ring kernels.
Arithmetic of Jindo's 255-bit coefficient field in a four-limb Montgomery representation. It is a prime-field owner of the commitment scheme, not an RNS ring kernel.

Goldilocks proof-field transform stage of the FASTPQ Metal backend, its dispatch and its scalar field helpers. It serves the STARK field and its acceleration contract, not an FHE ring, and stays with the shared proof backend.

CPU Goldilocks proof-field transforms of FASTPQ: the radix-2 transform with its scalar helpers (cyclotomic.rs), the trace and LDE planner (fft.rs) and the exact-root column transform with its CPU fallback (goldilocks_transform.rs). They transform STARK trace columns over the proof field, not an RLWE ring, and stay with the shared proof backend. specs/fastpq/shared_backend_inventory.json (task B.1) is the census of every Goldilocks owner.

Copies of Goldilocks proof-field arithmetic outside the FASTPQ crates: the u128-widening subtract, multiply and reduce helpers of the BFV full-bootstrap statement material in fhe_bfv.rs, and the scalar reduction of the Core native STARK verifier. They compute in the STARK proof field, not in an RLWE ring, so they do not move to iroha_fhe. fastpq_isi is the lowest listed crate that already holds this field arithmetic; B.3 moves the importers to the shared proof backend and C.8 replaces the BFV bootstrap material.

unrelated_kernel_named.reason: Trait method that reduces a 64-byte challenge into the scalar field of the generalized Bulletproof group; curve scalar arithmetic, not an RNS ring kernel.
Borrows a power-of-two prefix of the generator basis; no arithmetic.
Bound predicate on balanced coefficients of the Jindo response; it lifts nothing.

protocol_logic.component: Parameter sets, registered RAM-LFE profile and the production refusal
protocol_logic.note: q is a multiple of t and errors are multiples of t, so the public-key equation is noiseless modulo t. This profile is refused for production and is not renamed into the RNS-BGV candidate.

protocol_logic.component: Crate-private seeded key generation, encryption and error sampling
protocol_logic.note: pub(crate) and compiled unconditionally: `evaluate_bfv_affine` in ram_lfe.rs derives identifier key material from a seed, and the zero-refresh transcript validators re-derive rotation and bootstrap keys. Randomness is ChaCha20 seeded from a hash without a clearing RNG owner; C.3 replaces the distributions and randomness.

protocol_logic.component: Secret-key decryption and identifier slot decoding
protocol_logic.note: Diagnostic owner-side decryption; no verifiable decryption proof exists.

protocol_logic.component: Ciphertext addition, plaintext operations, multiplication and affine circuits
protocol_logic.note: Scheme logic over the shared kernels. Each operation exists in exact-residual, bounded-noise, RNS-exact and registered-chain variants.

protocol_logic.component: Galois key switching on ciphertexts and slot rotation
protocol_logic.note: Uses automorphism.galois and key_switch.digit_inner_product.

protocol_logic.component: Plaintext encoding and packed slot evaluation points
protocol_logic.note: Slot packing over the plaintext modulus. The measured F257 alternative is the test-only candidate recorded under test_only_references.

protocol_logic.component: Residual-multiple and bounded-noise output bounds, capacities and evaluation budgets
protocol_logic.note: Residual-multiple bounds of the exact-lift profile and bounds of the unqualified bounded-noise variant. C.3 derives the distributions and failure bounds of the replacement.

protocol_logic.component: Shape and metadata validation of keys, ciphertexts and polynomials, and secret-key consistency checks
protocol_logic.note: The secret-consistency checks recompute a key or ciphertext equation with the secret key; nothing here is a well-formedness proof.

protocol_logic.component: Canonical byte decoding and digests of public keys, ciphertexts and registered chains
protocol_logic.note: Norito decoding and digest binding of BFV material.

protocol_logic.component: Evaluation-key bundle validation, refresh-transcript validation and bundle digests
protocol_logic.note: Refresh-transcript validation re-derives rotation and bootstrap keys from seeds, and zero-refresh validation decrypts with the secret key.

protocol_logic.component: Refresh rounds, bootstrap-key validation and zero-refresh transcripts
protocol_logic.note: Refresh rounds add encrypted-zero masks under the exact-lift profile; they reduce no noise. Genuine bootstrapping is C.8 work.

protocol_logic.component: Governed full-bootstrap material, artifacts, linear-transform, blind-rotation and sample-extraction evaluators and their bounds
protocol_logic.note: Applies governed artifacts under the exact-lift profile. Adding bootstrap material to this profile does not repair it.

protocol_logic.component: Full-bootstrap proof-key material, native STARK/FRI payload encoders and their validators
protocol_logic.note: Key material and payload shapes for a proof that is not produced or verified here.

protocol_logic.component: Full-bootstrap execution claims, witness digests, proof and prover input material, arithmetic trace, AIR evaluation material and public-input schema
protocol_logic.note: Typed statement, trace and schema material of the full-bootstrap relation.

protocol_logic.component: Release-audit evidence, signoff, record, manifest and package predicates and their placeholder detectors
protocol_logic.note: Audit and reviewer-signature predicates that C.6 removes; they are not arithmetic and establish no proof.

protocol_logic.component: Public-key and ciphertext proof statements and input material
protocol_logic.note: Typed statement material; no well-formedness proof is produced or verified here.

protocol_logic.summary: Private adapters over iroha_fhe. Each binds BFV parameters (degree, q, t, decomposition base, the registered root table) to a shared kernel, keeps the BFV guard order and translates the typed arithmetic error into the BFV diagnostic. None holds an arithmetic body; `BfvRnsModulusChain` and `BfvRnsPolynomial` remain the BFV wire types.

BFV exactness policy and flows composed from the adapters: chain coverage bounds for exact Z_q addition and negacyclic products, the exact RNS corridors and centered scale-and-round of raw products, registered decomposition and source-chain selection, key switching and relinearization.

protocol_logic.component: Secret-key ownership, redaction and erasure
protocol_logic.note: Clearing owner for secret coefficients.

protocol_logic.component: Authenticated eight-party decryption transcript boundary
protocol_logic.note: Checks a public transcript and eight signatures over opaque commitments and releases no result. It is not a threshold decryption protocol; C.4 builds explicit thresholds and verifiable shares.

protocol_logic.component: Backend selection, policy commitments and the BFV affine and programmed evaluators
protocol_logic.note: `require_production_support` accepts only the HKDF backend and refuses both BFV backends; every encrypted consumer then rejects HKDF, so no backend has an effect. `evaluate_bfv_affine` derives identifier key material from a seed and decrypts the affine outputs.

protocol_logic.component: Plaintext HKDF-SHA3-512 PRF backend that R.6 retires
protocol_logic.note: Recorded under hkdf.ram_lfe_backend. It evaluates a keyed PRF on plaintext input and returns the normalized input as output.

protocol_logic.component: Plaintext keyed derivation of the network-scoped phone nullifier
protocol_logic.note: Recorded under hkdf.plaintext_prf. A genuine plaintext PRF, not encrypted evaluation and not a proven opening.

protocol_logic.component: Hidden-program validation and the register machine that evaluates it over BFV ciphertexts
protocol_logic.note: Executes the hidden tape with the BFV evaluator; refused for production with the BFV backends.

protocol_logic.component: Hidden-program codec and the clearing execution trace
protocol_logic.note: Canonical program bytes and the ciphertext trace owner; no arithmetic.

protocol_logic.component: Clearing owners of resolver secrets, affine circuits and policy-secret commitments
protocol_logic.note: Zeroizing owners and the secret commitment; no evaluation.

protocol_logic.component: Canonical V1 policy, function identity, query limit and commitment types
protocol_logic.note: Task R.0 owns this file; it defines commitments and limits, not evaluation.

protocol_logic.component: Program class membership and rank, multiplication and refresh accounting
protocol_logic.note: Structural accounting of a hidden program; logical ranks are not RNS levels.

protocol_logic.component: Deterministic derivation of initial memory lanes
protocol_logic.note: Hash expansion and reduction of lanes modulo the plaintext modulus.

protocol_logic.component: Cleartext reference semantics of the V1 program class
protocol_logic.note: Evaluates the program on plaintext scalars as the semantic reference; it encrypts nothing.

protocol_logic.component: Cleartext normal form of a V1 tape: the specification oracle of the normalizing lowering
protocol_logic.note: Folds the plaintext runs of a hidden tape into affine forms over F257 and keeps each multiplication, selection and scheduled refresh as one gate, on plaintext scalars; it encrypts nothing. The encrypted normalizer, its fixed public schedule and its proof belong to tasks R.3, R.7 and R.9.

protocol_logic.component: Provider-backed phone-control number commitment, provider key identity and provider signature rule
protocol_logic.note: Task R.1 owns this file. It commits a canonical E.164 number with the six-lane Goldilocks digest and checks provider signatures; it encrypts and evaluates nothing. The private relation over the commitment is task R.2 and State enforcement is task R.4.

protocol_logic.component: Multi-key RNS-BGV profile validation and digests
protocol_logic.note: T256 plaintext modulus and up to 64 RNS limbs; the resource certificate admits rosters of 2 to 8 parties. `BgvProfile::validate` checks limb primality and negacyclic roots with the duplicated `is_prime_u64` and `mod_pow`. `RnsPolynomial` is a production type whose arithmetic methods are #[cfg(test)].

protocol_logic.component: Release manifest, release evidence, readiness gates and fail-closed entry
protocol_logic.note: The production surface refuses until every gate closes; readiness predicates are removed with the activation gates, the missing relations remain work.

protocol_logic.component: Machine-checked noise bounds
protocol_logic.note: Distinct BGV multi-key noise semantics; stays with ZK-AMS.

protocol_logic.component: Resource ceilings, wire length certificates and evaluated-key layout accounting
protocol_logic.note: Counts ring multiplications and NTT work units without executing them.

protocol_logic.component: Security parameter candidate and frozen certificate
protocol_logic.note: Frozen security certificate bound to the profile's security parameters; distinct from the BFV profile.

protocol_logic.component: T256 slot packing layout, rotations and Galois key schedule
protocol_logic.note: Quadratic-extension arithmetic over the T256 base field for packing roots; protocol-specific, not a shared RNS kernel.

protocol_logic.component: Smudged decryption-share resource evidence and wide magnitude bounds
protocol_logic.note: Production computes sizes and bounds only; share generation, proofs and combination are #[cfg(test)].

protocol_logic.component: RNS-native proof topology, profile, proof digests, transcript roots and the move-only source arena
protocol_logic.note: RNS-native relation topology and candidate profile. The composite verifier module is #[cfg(test)]; the qPCS and phase II/III relation files keep only constants and types in production.

protocol_logic.component: ZK-AMS admission relation prove and verify entry points
protocol_logic.note: Both entry points call `require_mkhe_release_ready_v1` before proving or verifying. The readiness gates are open (the crate's tests assert `!is_ready()`), so both return ReleaseUnavailable.

protocol_logic.component: Phase II/III equation certificate, mask-proof, exact-binding and receipt-capability audits
protocol_logic.note: Audit and certificate records of relations that are not implemented in production; each reports its blockers.

protocol_logic.component: Drop, Debug and conversion impls of zeroizing and transport types
protocol_logic.note: Production keeps these type impls so the types exist; the code that uses them is #[cfg(test)].

protocol_logic.component: JindoRnsPolynomialV1 and its prime-modulus table
protocol_logic.note: The polynomial type keeps its methods and pinned primes; sums, differences and scaling call the shared slice kernels and the product calls the shared transform product.

protocol_logic.component: Unit-difference security certificate of the challenge set
protocol_logic.note: Checks challenge differences against the pinned primes with the shared scalar kernels of crates/iroha_fhe.

protocol_logic.component: Application and proof polynomial types of the degree-64 rings
protocol_logic.note: The polynomial types keep their methods, representation and clearing. Every ring operation of both rings, including the application-ring schoolbook product and scaling, runs on the shared branch-free fixed-modulus kernels of crates/iroha_fhe with this profile's pinned Montgomery constants; the module holds no arithmetic of its own. The remaining private functions bind the fixed ring degree, widen and narrow the u16 application residues, and translate a rejected shape.

protocol_logic.component: Quadratic constraint toolbox and commitment helpers
protocol_logic.note: Compiles and evaluates proof relations over the ring types.

protocol_logic.component: Parameter sets, the first-prime derivation rule, pinned candidates, canonical identity and the pinned evaluation context
protocol_logic.note: Candidates are starting points for measurement; none has a reviewed security estimate. Validation rejects any prime that is not 1 mod 2*N*t.

protocol_logic.component: Operating-system entropy, the BLAKE3 coin stream and the ternary, centered binomial and uniform samplers
protocol_logic.note: A failed or stuck entropy draw fails the operation. The seed, the hash state that absorbs it, the stream state and the buffered stream bytes live in one heap block that is overwritten whole before it is released; crates/iroha_fhe/tests/bgv_clearing.rs observes every such block.

protocol_logic.component: Secret, public, relinearization and Galois keys, their generators, their canonical word and byte encodings with decoders, and the custody frame of the secret key
protocol_logic.note: Generators that take an entropy source or explicit coins are pub(super); only the fixture module re-exports them. A decoded key is well formed as an encoding only: nothing here authenticates a frame or proves a key equation.

protocol_logic.component: Plaintexts, ciphertexts, public-key encryption, decryption and the canonical word and byte encodings
protocol_logic.note: The noise bound in a decoded frame is the sender's claim; the proofs that make it valid belong to the consumers.

protocol_logic.component: Addition, plaintext operations, tensor product, relinearization, hybrid key switching, automorphisms and modulus switching
protocol_logic.note: Every operation takes the shape of its result from rns_bgv.shape_planning and refuses a result whose public noise bound exceeds the capacity of its level.

protocol_logic.component: Public worst-case noise bounds and the decryption-failure condition
protocol_logic.note: Functions take public quantities only; no key, coin or decrypted value can reach a bound.

protocol_logic.component: Public shapes of ciphertexts (level, components, noise bound), the admission of every operation on them and the rule that lowers a product while its capacity ratio grows
protocol_logic.note: The evaluation module takes the level, component count and bound of every result from here, so a plan is the admission part of the evaluator run without residues. Takes no key, plaintext value or coin.

protocol_logic.component: Scalar slot encodings (sparse subalgebra and fully split batching), slot masks, slot movement and the broadcast
protocol_logic.note: Subalgebra membership of a hidden plaintext needs a proof from whoever encrypted it; that proof is task R.11.

protocol_logic.component: Deterministic sizes and work units from public profile geometry; every size is the length of a frame the crate encodes
protocol_logic.note: scripts/fhe_bgv_cost_model.py holds an independent model and checks specs/fhe_bgv_cost_summary.json against it; crates/iroha_fhe/tests/bgv_cost_model_vectors.rs recomputes the sizes, work units, instruction costs, tape plans and contract inputs of that summary with this module, the noise rules and the costing harness.

protocol_logic.component: Limb-major residue polynomial in a clearing owner, with limb-wise transforms and arithmetic on the shared kernels
protocol_logic.note: Holds no kernel of its own: every operation calls iroha_fhe::ntt_plan, iroha_fhe::constant_time or iroha_fhe::automorphism.

protocol_logic.component: The scheme error type and its conversions from kernel errors
protocol_logic.note: Kernel errors collapse to one variant: they indicate an internal shape error, never an input the caller chose.

protocol_logic.component: Named points at which a test can make a secret-handling operation unwind
protocol_logic.note: In a production build `reached` compiles to nothing; `arm` and `disarm` exist only with the fixture feature.

test_only_references.summary: Known-answer vectors for every primitive, derived with Python integers, and a num-bigint oracle built from the textbook definitions that re-derives each one. It shares no code with the kernels. Rounding, modulus-switch, automorphism and digit vectors include the registered ciphertext modulus 257 * 2^48.
Inline unit tests of the shared kernels, including the scalar model of the vector Montgomery reduction and the direct tests of the AVX2 kernel.

Portable model of the twelve AVX2 intrinsics the AVX2 kernel uses. Hosts without AVX2 compile the kernel against it, so its schedule is compared with the scalar reference everywhere; x86-64 hosts compare each modelled intrinsic with the CPU. It models instruction semantics and shares no code with the scalar kernels.
Integration test whose allocator inspects freed blocks: kernel scratch holding operand copies or partial results is all zero when released, after success, a rejected input and an unwind.
Inline unit tests of the RNS-BGV modules.

Seeded entropy, explicit-coin entry points, secret-derived probes and fault arming. Compiled only for tests or with the bgv-test-fixtures feature, which no production dependency edge enables; not a production stack.

Run-time num-bigint reference of the whole scheme on integers modulo the full modulus (schoolbook or Kronecker products, constructive CRT, rounding rules from their definitions, its own coin derivation and samplers). Shares no code with iroha_fhe.

Pure-Python reference with its own single-chunk BLAKE3 that generates tests/vectors/bgv_kat_v1.txt: chain conversion and scale-down vectors over 18 fifty-bit and 6 sixty-bit primes and three complete seeded pipelines.

Requires the crate to reproduce every pinned word of the Python reference and every step of the num-bigint oracle on several chain shapes, including the affine candidate at N = 2^14, and to decode its keys from the pinned words into the frames it encodes.

Compares the public noise bound with the exact noise the oracle computes: the fresh bound attained exactly, the capacity boundary, the modulus-switch bound within one unit and random admitted sequences.

Allocator probe: every polynomial-sized block released by key generation, encryption, decryption, the encodings and the secret-key custody frame, and every block that held the seed and stream state of an operation, is all zero after success, an error return and an unwind.

One lowering of the eleven V1 tape instructions onto the scheme with two back ends, public shapes and ciphertexts, the ledger of operations, work units and live buffers, an independent cleartext machine and the maximum-shape tape families. A costing harness for tests and measurements, not an evaluator a consumer has adopted.

The planned and the encrypted run of one tape agree on every level and noise bound instruction by instruction, the encrypted run computes the tape, the ledger charges each instruction its lowering, and the equality indicator is exact for all 257 field values under encryption.

Recomputes the candidates' geometry, sizes and work units, the instruction costs, every tape-family plan and the contract inputs of specs/fhe_bgv_cost_summary.json, through its generated view, with the Rust cost model, noise rules, slot encoding and costing harness; every key of the view has to be read by a check.

ram_lfe_backend.summary: `HkdfSha3_512PrfV1` is a plaintext keyed PRF backend. It is the only backend `require_production_support` accepts and Core registers its policies, yet every encrypted consumer rejects it, so it is accepted without effect. `evaluate_hkdf_prf` returns the normalized input as its output. It is not encrypted evaluation and not a live Torii fallback.
ram_lfe_backend.replacement: The canonical class-bound V1 policy from R.0 replaces `RamLfeBackend`; the old tag then rejects at Norito and JSON decoding and at registration, without an alias.
